requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
**Implementation**

The Rust profile in `src/outline/rust.rs` implements every obligation in the requirement.

- **Outline nodes (`const[KINDS]`):** it maps these kinds, and only these, to outline nodes:
  - `function_item` and `function_signature_item` to `fn`. This covers functions, methods and trait method signatures.
  - `struct_item`, `enum_item`, `union_item`, `trait_item` and `mod_item`.
  - `impl_item`.
  - `macro_definition`, plus `macro_invocation` in item position.
  - `const_item`, `static_item`, and `type_item` with `associated_type`.
  - `foreign_mod_item` as `extern`.
  - `extern_crate_declaration` and `use_declaration`.
- **Named by field:** most kinds are named by their `name` field, which gives selectors such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]` and `mod[local]/fn[run]`.
- **Ancestry:** the general outline machinery nests nodes, so `fn[outer]/fn[inner]` and `mod[local]/fn[run]` follow syntactic ancestry within one file.
- **Impls (`impl_name`):** the name is the self type's source text. When a `trait` field is present, the trait path is added as a second part, which gives `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. Generics are kept as written, for example `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.
- **Extern blocks (`extern_name`):** the name is the ABI string, or `Rust` when there is none.
- **Anonymous items:** `use_declaration` and item-position macro invocations use `NameRule::Anonymous`. `item_macro` and `in_item_list` restrict macro nodes to item position, so expression macros inside function bodies are not nodes.
- **No cross-file resolution:** nothing in the profile resolves modules across files. `mod external;` is a plain `mod[external]` leaf.
- **Documentation:** `md/reference.md` documents the selector spelling and a Rust profile table. It covers the examples, `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`, anonymous `use@…` and macros, ABI naming, percent-encoding, `#N` disambiguation, and "Modules are never resolved across files".
- **Marking:** all helper functions that carry out this requirement carry `{impl}`: `impl_name`, `extern_name`, `in_item_list`, `item_macro`, `KINDS` and `PROFILE`. The other helpers in the file implement comments and hashing, which belong to other requirements, so they do not need this marker.

Two minor points, neither a blocking gap. `extern-crate` and `function_signature_item` are mapped though not listed by name in the requirement. Both are named items, are documented in the profile table, and fit the requirement's intent.

**Tests**

- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` checks selectors and round-trip resolution for:
  - inline and external `mod`, `struct`, inherent and trait impls;
  - an impl on an array type, whose name is percent-encoded as `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`;
  - trait methods and associated types;
  - `extern "C"` and a bare `extern`, which becomes `extern[Rust]`;
  - nested fns and duplicate `fn[repeated]#1` and `#2`;
  - `macro_rules!`, `union`, `enum`, `const`, `static`, `type` and `extern crate`.

  It also checks that the root selector `""` resolves, and that an ambiguous selector and a missing selector are errors.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` checks anonymous `use@` selectors that differ between two uses, along with most of the same named cases.
- `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` checks that item-position macros are anonymous, at top level and inside impl and mod bodies. It also checks that macros inside function bodies and a `println!()` in expression position are not nodes, and that a generic impl is named `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.
- `nodes_are_declared_on_their_name_line_or_where_their_syntax_starts` covers the multi-line impl header and `extern "system"` cases. It cites `requirements.cli.add_input_item` rather than this requirement, so it adds only supporting coverage.

The tests cover the main cases and edge cases. No FIXME gaps are acknowledged or needed.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
